description: Taking these together increases the risk of serious bleeding.
source: FDA label: Jantoven (warfarin) §5.1, §7.3
evidence_check: supported. No change.

description: Ibuprofen with warfarin increases the risk of serious bleeding, including in the stomach.
source: FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions); FDA label: Jantoven (warfarin) §5.1, §7.3
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Optional: add liver_function:impaired (advanced liver disease raises GI-bleed risk).

description: Naproxen with warfarin increases the risk of serious bleeding, including in the stomach.
source: FDA label: Naprosyn (naproxen) §5.2, §7 Table 1; FDA label: Jantoven (warfarin) §5.1, §7.3
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Optional: add liver_function:impaired.

description: Using two blood-thinning medicines together increases the risk of serious bleeding.
source: FDA label: Plavix (clopidogrel) §7.5; FDA label: Jantoven (warfarin) §5.1, §7.3
evidence_check: supported. No change; second citation added.

description: Clarithromycin greatly raises simvastatin levels, increasing the risk of severe muscle damage.
source: FDA label: Zocor (simvastatin) §4, §5.1, §7.1 Table 2
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Clarithromycin is named in Zocor §7.1 Table 2 as a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (the class contraindicated in §4).

description: Clarithromycin raises atorvastatin levels and can increase the risk of muscle damage. The atorvastatin dose may need to be limited.
source: FDA label: Lipitor (atorvastatin) §2.5, §5.1, §7.1
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Added kidney_function:impaired; description now mentions the dose limit. Reviewer: Severity borderline Moderate/Major (label caps atorvastatin at 20 mg with clarithromycin). Kept Moderate.

description: Both medicines can raise potassium; together they can cause dangerously high potassium levels.
source: FDA label: Zestril (lisinopril) §7.1; FDA label: Aldactone (spironolactone) §5.1; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 5
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: age_range:65_plus is indirect (older people more often have reduced kidney function).

description: Ibuprofen can weaken the blood-pressure-lowering effect of lisinopril, and together they can harm the kidneys.
source: FDA label: Zestril (lisinopril) §7.3; FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions)
evidence_check: supported. No change.

description: Naproxen can weaken the blood-pressure-lowering effect of lisinopril, and together they can harm the kidneys.
source: FDA label: Naprosyn (naproxen) §7 Table 1
evidence_check: supported. No change.

description: Omeprazole can stop clopidogrel from working properly, raising the risk of clots. Doctors usually avoid this combination and may choose a different stomach medicine.
source: FDA label: Plavix (clopidogrel) §5.1, §7.2
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Severity Moderate -> Major; description rewritten. Reviewer: FDA warning covers omeprazole and esomeprazole only; consider adding an esomeprazole + clopidogrel rule.

description: Metoclopramide blocks dopamine and can counteract levodopa, which may worsen Parkinson's symptoms.
source: FDA label: Reglan (metoclopramide) §5.1, §5.2, §7.2; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 3
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Label says avoid (not contraindicated), so Major. Support for the age factor is general only.

description: Ibuprofen may interfere with the heart-protective effect of low-dose aspirin, and together they raise the risk of stomach bleeding.
source: FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions); FDA label: Naprosyn (naproxen) §5.2
evidence_check: supported. No change.

description: Together these increase the risk of bleeding. They are often prescribed together on purpose, so discuss this with your doctor.
source: FDA label: Plavix (clopidogrel) §1.1, §6.1, §7.7; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 2
evidence_check: supported. No change.

description: Ibuprofen can reduce the effect of furosemide and increase the risk of kidney problems.
source: FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions); FDA label: Lasix (furosemide)
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Added age_range:65_plus.

description: These medicines have opposite effects on the same body signals, so each may work less well.
source: FDA label: Aricept (donepezil) §7.1; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 7
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Could be argued Major (Beers: avoid anticholinergics in dementia).

description: When the kidneys are not working well, metformin can build up and raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis.
source: FDA label: metformin HCl tablets, Boxed Warning, §4, §8.7
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Severity Contraindicated -> Major; added liver_function:impaired. Reviewer: Label contraindication is eGFR < 30 only; starting at 30-45 is not recommended. A coarse 'impaired' flag cannot tell these apart. The FDA 2016 safety communication could not be opened.

description: Ibuprofen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
source: FDA label: ibuprofen tablets Rx (Precautions, Drug Interactions); AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Optional: add liver_function:impaired. Threshold CrCl < 30 (Beers).

description: Naproxen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
source: FDA label: naproxen tablets §5.6, §8.5, §8.7; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Optional: add liver_function:impaired. Threshold CrCl < 30.

description: Simvastatin should not be used in active or severe liver disease, and needs caution with other liver problems, because it can further affect the liver.
source: FDA label: Zocor (simvastatin) §4; UK SmPC: Simvastatin 20 mg §4.3
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Severity Contraindicated -> Major; description rewritten. Reviewer: US label now contraindicates only acute liver failure / decompensated cirrhosis; UK SmPC still says active liver disease.

description: Liver disease can make paracetamol more likely to cause liver harm.
source: UK SmPC: Paracetamol 500 mg Tablets (Zentiva) §4.4; FDA label: Ofirmev (acetaminophen) §5.1
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: IV label contraindicates severe hepatic impairment; oral SmPC says caution only.

description: In older adults, oxybutynin is more likely to cause confusion, constipation and other side effects.
source: FDA label: oxybutynin chloride tablets (Precautions, Geriatric Use); AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 7
evidence_check: supported-with-changes. Added liver_function:impaired.

description: With reduced kidney function, spironolactone can cause high potassium levels.
source: FDA label: Aldactone (spironolactone) §5.1, §8.5, §8.6; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 6
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Major rests on Beers Table 6 (avoid if CrCl < 30); the label itself says monitor potassium.

description: Children and teenagers are more likely to get movement-related side effects from metoclopramide.
source: FDA label: Reglan (metoclopramide) §5.2, §8.4; EMA press release 2013-07-26
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Optional: mention long-lasting movement problems (tardive dyskinesia). EU: contraindicated under 1 year.

rule: Calcium channel blocker -> ankle and leg swelling (oedema) -> Loop diuretic
description: Medicines like amlodipine can cause ankle swelling, which is sometimes treated with a water tablet (diuretic) instead of reviewing the original medicine.
source: McCarthy 2022 ThinkCascades (Drugs Aging); Savage 2020 (JAMA Intern Med)
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: ThinkCascades says 'diuretics' generally; the rule only matches loop diuretics. On the final ThinkCascades list.

rule: Cholinesterase inhibitor -> new urinary incontinence -> Antimuscarinic
description: Dementia medicines like donepezil can cause bladder leakage, which is sometimes treated with a bladder medicine that may work against the dementia medicine.
source: Gill 2005 (Arch Intern Med)
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Not on the final ThinkCascades list (round 1 only). Memantine could be added as a trigger.

rule: Metoclopramide -> Parkinson-like movement symptoms -> Antiparkinson agent
description: Metoclopramide can cause shaking or stiffness that looks like Parkinson's disease, which is sometimes treated with Parkinson's medicine.
source: Avorn 1995 (JAMA)
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Not on the final ThinkCascades list. Prochlorperazine could be added as a trigger.

rule: NSAID -> raised blood pressure -> ACE inhibitor / Calcium channel blocker
description: Anti-inflammatory painkillers can raise blood pressure, which is sometimes treated with a new blood-pressure medicine.
source: McCarthy 2022 ThinkCascades (Drugs Aging); Gurwitz 1994 (JAMA)
evidence_check: supported. No change. Reviewer: Evidence covers any antihypertensive; the rule only matches ACE inhibitors and CCBs. On the final ThinkCascades list.
